{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Richard Neil Lyons''' (born January 22, 1945, in [[New York City]], [[New York (state)|New York]])<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.math.uic.edu/~ronan/The_mathematicians |title=Mathematicians who classified finite simple groups |access-date=March 28, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110924004209/http://www.math.uic.edu/~ronan/The_mathematicians |archive-date=September 24, 2011 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> is an American mathematician specializing in finite group theory.

Lyons received his PhD in 1970 at the [[University of Chicago]] under [[John Griggs Thompson]] with the thesis ''Characterizations of Some Finite Simple Groups with Small 2-Rank''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=6626}}</ref> From 1972 to 2017, he was a professor at [[Rutgers University]].

With [[Daniel Gorenstein]] and [[Ronald Solomon]] he wrote, and is continuing to write, now with [[Inna Capdeboscq]], a series on the second-generation proof of the [[Classification of finite simple groups|classification program for finite simple groups]]. Ten volumes of this series have been published so far. He discovered a [[sporadic group]]<ref>Richard Lyons (1972,5) "Evidence for a new finite simple group", [[Journal of Algebra]] 20:540&ndash;569, and 34:188&ndash;189</ref> which [[Charles Sims (mathematician)|Charles Sims]] constructed and called the [[Lyons group]] ''Ly''.

In 2012, he shared the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Mathematical Exposition, awarded by the American Mathematical Society, with [[Michael Aschbacher]], Stephen D. Smith, and Ronald Solomon.
In 2013, he became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to the classification of the finite simple groups, including the discovery of one of the 26 sporadic finite simple groups.".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |access-date=January 28, 2015 |archive-date=August 25, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Works ==
* with Gorenstein: ''The local structure of finite groups of characteristic 2 type'', American Mathematical Society, 1983
* with Daniel Gorenstein, Ronald Solomon: ''The classification of the finite simple groups'', American Mathematical Society, 10 Vols., 1994–2023
* with Michael Aschbacher, Stephen D. Smith, Ronald Solomon: ''The classification of finite simple groups: Groups of characteristic 2 type'', American Mathematical Society, 2011
